item.title: Odd Lots: Branko Milanovic on the New Economic Order (Podcast)
item.description: It’s pretty obvious by now that globalization has fallen out of favor. And while many pundits have deemed economic globalism dead, we are still figuring out what to call this new era. Branko Milanovic’s chosen phrase is “national market liberalism,” a term that sums up how a world once defined by the free movement of capital has begun to contract as the most powerful governments have come to favor mercantilism and nationalism. item.title: Kazimir Says ECB Must Hike at Least Once More to Quell Inflation
item.description: The European Central Bank will have to raise interest rates at least one more time to ensure that inflation risks don’t spin out of control, according to Governing Council member Peter Kazimir.

item.title: AT&T Kick Starts Sale of Five-Part Euro, Sterling Bond Deal
item.description: AT&T Inc. has opened books on a at least €2 billion ($2.23 billion) euro and sterling bond offering, injecting a large corporate deal into what’s a traditionally subdued period for Europe’s primary market.

item.title: Audi Turns Gloomier on Sales Outlook Due to Downturn in China
item.description: The Audi group sees lower sales and profitability this year as worsening conditions in China and US tariffs hamper the carmaker’s turnaround efforts.

item.title: Multiverse Raising Funds at $1.7 Billion Value to Cut AI Costs
item.description: Multiverse Computing SL is raising $570 million in a funding round that is set to boost its valuation to $1.7 billion, as investors flock to companies aiming to make it cheaper to use artificial intelligence.

item.title: First US LNG Shipment to China in a Year to Be Re-Exported
item.description: The first US liquefied natural gas shipment to China in more than a year will be re-exported, as the local companies involved look to tap higher profits overseas and avoid paying tariffs, according to people with knowledge of the matter.

item.title: Asia-Bound Tanker Exits Red Sea Via Suez as Others Risk Strait
item.description: An Asia-bound supertanker carrying Saudi oil has exited the Red Sea via the longer Suez Canal route while other vessels continue to risk the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, as Houthi threats heighten uncertainty in the region.

item.title: Vodafone Service Revenue Beats Estimates on German Growth
item.description: Vodafone Group Plc reported first-quarter service revenue growth that beat analysts’ estimates after sales increased in Germany, the phone carrier’s largest market.

item.description: Vodacom Group Ltd. trimmed its dividend-payout plan and raised its revenue, earnings and cash-flow goals as the wireless carrier seeks to reinvest capital in its higher-growth eastern and northern African businesses.

item.title: Soybean Oil Drops Most in Month After US Halts Strikes on Iran
item.description: Chicago soybean oil futures fell the most in a month on Monday as the US pause in strikes against Iran eased fears of further escalation, sending crude prices tumbling and pulling grain and oilseed markets lower.

item.title: Innolight Is Said Set to Price Hong Kong Listing Below Maximum
item.description: Zhongji Innolight Co. is telling prospective investors it is on track to price its HK$53.4 billion ($6.8 billion) Hong Kong listing below the maximum, according to people familiar with the matter, as the company moves closer to sealing the city’s biggest first-time share sale in seven years.

item.title: India Lured $40 Billion Since June, Malhotra Tells BusinessLine
item.description: India’s push to attract overseas capital has brought in nearly $40 billion since June, strengthening the country’s external buffers as policymakers seek to slow the rupee’s decline.

item.title: China State Media Says Support for Open AI Models Has Limits
item.description: China should restrict access to the most powerful features of artificial intelligence models, a state media commentary suggested, highlighting limits to Beijing’s support for open technology.

item.title: SoftBank’s $40 Billion Loan for OpenAI Stake Gets 21 New Lenders
item.description: SoftBank Group Corp.’s $40 billion bridge loan for its investment in US tech giant OpenAI has attracted a new group of 21 lenders in a broader syndication phase, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: CXMT Can Rally More Than 1,200% on Market Share Win, Nomura Says
item.description: China’s memory-chip bellwether CXMT Corp. can extend its blockbuster stock market debut to rally 1,239% from its initial public offering price as it wins market share over time, according to Nomura Holdings Inc.

item.title: Australian Fuel Prices Jump Most Since March as Iran Truce Wilts
item.description: Australian gasoline prices jumped last week by the most since the height of the US-Iran war following the collapse of a ceasefire between Washington and Tehran, suggesting persistent inflationary pressures ahead.

item.title: Indonesia’s Acting Central Bank Chief Damayanti Seen as Reassuring for Investors
item.description: Destry Damayanti, announced as acting chief of Bank Indonesia Monday, is a trained economist whose monetary policy experience may comfort investors rattled by the sudden resignation of Governor Perry Warjiyo.

item.title: Warjiyo’s Departure Raises Scrutiny on BI Policy, Analysts Say
item.description: Bank Indonesia Governor Perry Warjiyo’s resignation is expected to heighten uncertainty and volatility across the nation’s financial markets, with analysts citing concerns over policy direction and central bank independence.

item.title: CATL Surges After Share Buyback Plan, Strong First-Half Profit
item.description: Contemporary Amperex Technology Co. Ltd. shares jumped in China after the world’s biggest electric-vehicle battery manufacturer unveiled a buyback plan following strong earnings for the first half.

item.title: Trip.com Shares Jump in Hong Kong as Regulatory Overhang Clears
item.description: Trip.com Group Ltd. posted its biggest gain in nearly a year after the outcome of its antitrust investigation largely matched expectations, lifting a key overhang on the stock even as the company was hit with a hefty fine.

item.title: India Retail Investors Cash Out as Foreign Buying of Stocks Resumes
item.description: Selling by retail investors could limit potential upside in the Nifty benchmark.

item.title: Instagram, Facebook Ran AI ‘Nudify’ Ads from China, Report Says
item.description: Meta Platforms Inc.’s Facebook and Instagram have served thousands of ads for AI “nudify” apps in breach of the company’s policies, delivered by one of its few advertising partners in China, according to the nonprofit Tech Transparency Project.

item.title: China Chipmakers See 2,580% Profit Jump as Economic Split Widens
item.description: China’s industry saw profit gains slow for a second month even as sectors benefiting from the tech boom enjoy a windfall, adding to evidence of an uneven recovery for companies across parts of the world’s second-biggest economy.
